title: Tiered throttle curve and shift playlist — rollout proposal (Nov 2026)
body:
Purpose:
This is a concise working proposal for a tiered traffic-throttle curve and a staffing/shift playlist to run a medium-risk model rollout on hosted API next month. Goal is to keep total customer-impact minutes low while exercising the new batching path and KV-cache hotfix.

Scope: hosted-api region: us-west1, model: rwd-infer-v2-quant (internal), rollout window: Nov 8–14 (primary), Nov 15–21 (contingency soak).

Quick TL;DR:
- Use a 6-step, exponentially increasing throttle curve instead of linear ramp to give faster rollback signal at low traffic and predictable tail-latency exposure.
- Staff a compact 3-person core ops pod per 12h window + 1 SRE floater for 24/7 first 72h.
- Preflight checklist must complete: smoke tests, traffic-replay sanity, KV-cache eviction sim, and billing-rate guardrails.
- Rollback triggers: 3x baseline 95th latency, 5% error rate delta vs baseline for 5 minutes, or any customer-facing 5xx spike > 60s.

Proposed throttle curve (percent of pre-rollout traffic sent to new model):
- phase-0 (warmup): 0.1% for 10m -> verify no 5xx, warm caches
- phase-1: 0.5% for 20m -> observe per-route p50/p95 and token cost variance
- phase-2: 2% for 30m -> watch batching size distribution and GPU util
- phase-3: 10% for 45m -> check latency tail and autoscaler behaviour
- phase-4: 40% for 90m -> longer soak, run A/B eval hooks
- phase-5: 100% progressive cutover (if all green) or cap at 60% and re-evaluate

Heuristic notes on step durations: these are intentionally front-loaded to gather high-signal fast; if any medium-severity alerts arise we stop and triage before next step.

Staffing playlist (ops shifts / primary responsibilities):
- Core pod (12h): Release Lead (exec decisions), Runtime SRE (latency/infra), Observability Engineer (dashboards/alerts).
- Night floater (24h cadence): On-call SRE available to escalate hardware or network issues.
- Second-week soak: reduce to 8h weekday coverage + async monitoring.

Concrete shift roster (first 72h):
- Day shift (0800–2000 PST): Aisha (lead), Miguel (runtime), Priya (obs)
- Night shift (2000–0800 PST): Evelyn (lead), SRE-floater rotation (TBD), Priya (obs - async)
- Pager escalation: severity-1 -> phone; severity-2 -> Slack #release-ops; severity-3 -> ticket with paging list

Preflight checklist (must be green before phase-0):
- [ ] Canary infra provisioned with identical GPU instance types (ticket: RI-4199)
- [ ] Model artifacts validated (sha256: provided in linked PR)
- [ ] Smoke tests: token-generation under concurrency=8, 10 runs each route
- [ ] Replay job: 1 hour production-capture replay at 2% sampling -> compare p95/p99
- [ ] KV-cache eviction simulation: run cache-thrash harness for 15m
- [ ] Billing guard: cost cap rule in console set to 1.2x baseline for first 24h
- [ ] Alert thresholds staged in staging and mirrored to prod alerts (docs: CONFLUENCE RI-release/alerts)
- [ ] Runbook pointer in Slack pinned message and Confluence link added to #release-ops

Telemetry gates (what to watch and gates to fail on):
- Latency: p95 > baseline_p95 * 3 => immediate rollback
- Errors: 5xx rate delta > +5% absolute over baseline for 5m => pause rollout and investigate
- Client-visible anomalies: any customer notice (payment or auth failures) => immediate rollback and incident bridge
- Cost <> token economics: per-token cost > baseline * 1.5 sustained for 30m => hold and consult Optimize team

Quick diagnostic checklist for runtime SRE (if alert fires):
1) Check GPU memory and NVLINK errors on node -> run nvidia-smi, dmesg
2) Confirm batching queues: queue-length, average batch size, inter-batch delay
3) KV cache hit ratio, eviction logs
4) Trace a single problematic request via trace-id -> identify model variant fallbacks
5) If hotspot, throttle at routing layer back to stable variant, notify Release Lead

Rollback plan & post-rollback steps:
- Fast rollback: reroute 100% to previous pinned model version and mark new version as quarantined.
- Post-rollback: capture 30m of raw traces, snapshot offending nodes, create P0 postmortem if SLI breach.
- Communicate: send status to #customers-critical and triage via customer-success.

Contingency lanes (if autoscaler thrashes):
- Reduce max replicas to baseline and enable burst queue drain; contact infra to pre-provision one extra GPU cluster; if queue backlog persists >10m escalate to oncall infra manager.

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Who is floater on Nov 9–10 night shift? @Evelyn please confirm.
- Confirm exact model sha256 and add to this doc + release PR.
- Decide whether to include quantized 8-bit variant in phase-3 for cost comparisons (Pros: cheaper, Cons: potential quality regressions).
- Baking: should we run synthetic high-token prompts during phase-2 to exercise KV-cache long histories? Need ops sign-off.

Communications plan:
- Pre-roll email to internal GTM + CS at phase-1 start with expected customer-visible risk = low.
- Customer-facing release note drafted by CS (attached as linked artifact RI-4128).
- Slack: #release-ops will host pinned runbook and live log stream; #alerts -> routed incidents.

Notes to self / rough scribbles:
- If p95 jumps with no 5xx, likely batching spike -> check recent infra kernel selection change in PR 987
- Keep an eye on embedding requests (different token distribution) if any test traffic leaks
- Consider keeping a manual circuit-breaker ready in routing policy for region fallback

Appendix: mini calendar (local PST)
- Nov 8 07:00: final preflight sync, gate signoff 07:45, phase-0 go/no-go 08:00
- Nov 8 08:00–12:00: phases 0–2 (warmup + small ramp)
- Nov 8 12:00–18:00: phases 3–4 (large ramp, soak)
- Nov 8 18:00–Nov 11 06:00: longer soak and monitoring, 12h core shifts as outlined
- Nov 12–14: decision window for 100% cutover or extended canary; if green cut Nov 14 10:00

Contact / signoff:
- Proposed by: Aisha Rahman (release engineering)
- Reviewed by: Miguel Santos, Priya Kapoor (obs), Evelyn Cho (SRE)

-- end working draft --
